bihar_raw_news.title: How the Bihar CM's orders come with a cyber memory - India Today
bihar_raw_news.content: Home India Today Insight How the Bihar CM’s orders come with a cyber memory Get 37% off on an annual Print +Digital subscription of India Today Magazine SUBSCRIBE How the Bihar CM's orders come with a cyber memory The Bihar government now has a digital dashboard to ensure no instruction is forgotten, and a portal to monitor coordination with the Centre advertisement Amitabh Srivastava UPDATED: Oct 15, 2026 19:24 IST Edited By: Satyadeep Samrat Choudhary can give a direction and move on. The system, at least in theory, will not forget. On October 13, the Bihar chief minister launched the Sankalp Dashboard and Samanvay Portal, putting the work of all 48 government departments on a common digital platform and creating a system to track what follows from his instructions, Cabinet decisions and important government communications. The idea is straightforward: a direction recorded in a review meeting should not disappear into a file—or be lost to bureaucratic memory. It should remain on the dashboard until the department concerned can show what action has been taken. advertisement Read More Launched at the chief secretariat’s Samvad auditorium, the Sankalp Dashboard brings together information on the principal functions and major projects of all 48 departments. It has six broad modules: CM-level monitoring; projects and investment; departmental presentations; performance and ranking; coordination and escalation; and field and public contact. More than 20 sub-modules will track information relating to government schemes, projects and departmental work. The dashboard will also record follow-up to directions issued by the chief minister during review meetings, government announcements, decisions of the Council of Ministers and important official communications. Departmental presentations and briefing material will also be available on the platform. The companion Samanvay Portal has a different but complementary purpose: monitoring coordination between the Bihar government and the Centre. It will track centrally sponsored schemes, the utilisation of funds received from the Union government, national rankings and important matters requiring coordination between the two governments. Bihar’s resident commissioner in Delhi will oversee the coordination mechanism. advertisement Choudhary said the two platforms would ensure “integrated, time-bound and result-oriented monitoring” of important government business. He also emphasised that funds received from the Centre should be utilised on time and that centrally sponsored schemes should be implemented effectively. Why this matters For a chief minister and the top administrative leadership, one of the perennial problems of governance is not necessarily the absence of decisions but the distance between a decision and its execution. A government can announce a scheme, approve a project or issue a direction in a review meeting, but implementation then passes through several layers of the bureaucracy. Files move between departments, approvals are sought, funds have to be released, tenders floated, agencies coordinated and field officials mobilised. At each stage, momentum can weaken. A decision that appeared urgent at the top can gradually become another item in a long administrative queue. This is where a monitoring system becomes important. bihar_raw_news.title: JEEViKA Marks 20 Years of Rural Transformation in Bihar - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next JEEViKA Marks 20 Years of Rural Transformation in Bihar 15 Oct 2026 2 min read Why in News? Bihar’s JEEViKA, the Bihar Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society (BRLPS), has completed 20 years, strengthening rural livelihoods, women’s financial inclusion and entrepreneurship through self-help groups (SHGs). Key Points Bihar Rural Livelihoods Project (JEEViKA) About: The Government of Bihar, through the Bihar Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society (BRLPS), an autonomous body under the Department of Rural Development, implements the Bihar Rural Livelihoods Project (BRLP), popularly known as JEEViKA, to promote the social and economic empowerment of rural poor. The core strategy of the BRLP programme is to build vibrant and bankable women’s community institutions in the form of self help groups (SHGs), who through member savings, internal loaning and regular repayment become self sustaining organizations. Status: JEEViKA has expanded from 6 self-help groups across 6 blocks to a statewide community network . Network Coverage : 1.81 crore households linked to 13.06 lakh SHGs. Community Institutions: 77,787 Gram Sangathans and 1,683 Cluster-Level Federations. Bank Credit: ₹76,549 crore accessed through SHGs. 6,771 Bank Sakhis facilitate banking services, financial transactions and financial awareness in rural areas. JEEViKA Didi Ki Rasoi: Promotes women’s participation in food services and institutional catering. bihar_raw_news.content: The Bihar Combined Entrance Competitive Examination Board (BCECEB) has released the opening and closing ranks for Round 3 of the Undergraduate Medical Admission Counselling (UGMAC) 2026 on October 14, 2026. This round offered 618 MBBS and 23 BDS vacant seats across government medical and dental colleges in Bihar. Candidates who have been allotted a seat must now complete document verification and admission formalities within a tight two-day window. For NEET-UG aspirants targeting a government MBBS or BDS seat in Bihar, this is often the final opportunity under state counselling before the mop-up round begins. If you were allotted a seat in Bihar UGMAC Round 3, you must report for document verification on October 16 or 17, 2026, at your allotted college, or your seat will be cancelled. Unlock My College List What Was Released and When On October 14, 2026, BCECEB published the provisional seat allotment result for Round 3, which includes the opening and closing ranks for each college, course, and category. These ranks determine which candidates have been assigned a seat and at which institution. The cutoff lists are now available on the official BCECEB portal at bceceboard.bihar.gov.in. Round 3 is the third and typically the final state-level counselling round in Bihar before the mop-up phase. The seats offered in this round come from vacancies left over after Rounds 1 and 2—these include seats that were not filled, candidates who did not report, or seats that became available due to upgrades and resignations. How Many Seats Were Available in Round 3 BCECEB released a total of 618 MBBS seats and 23 BDS seats for Round 3 across Bihar's government medical and dental colleges. These seats were distributed among eight major government medical colleges in the state, including Patna Medical College and Hospital (PMCH), Nalanda Medical College and Hospital (NMCH), Darbhanga Medical College and Hospital (DMCH), Sri Krishna Medical College and Hospital (SKMCH), Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College (JLNMCH), Anugrah Narayan Magadh Medical College (ANMMCH), Government Medical College Bettiah, and Government Medical College Chhapra. Veterinary seats under the BVSc programme were also included in the Round 3 seat matrix. The seat pool was open only to candidates who had cleared NEET UG 2026 and met Bihar's domicile and category eligibility requirements. Critical Dates You Must Know for Round 3 The Round 3 counselling process followed a compressed timeline. Registration and application opened on October 3 and closed on October 6, 2026. Candidates were required to fill and lock their college choices by October 9. The rank cards were published on October 8, giving aspirants one day to review their scores before finalising their preferences. bihar_raw_news.title: Taller Than Eiffel Tower, Chenab Rail Bridge To Get Touristy With Viewing Decks & Museum
bihar_raw_news.content: Homepage Trending Taller Than Eiffel Tower, Chenab Rail Bridge To Get Touristy With Viewing Decks & Museum Ashmeet Guliani On October 15, 2026, 12:44 PM Cover Image Courtesy: Chenab Rail Bridge/Wikipedia, Ministry of Railways Built over the Chenab River in the Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir, India, the Chenab Rail Bridge is considered the world’s highest railway arch bridge. And now, it is all set to be developed into a new tourist destination, with viewing platforms that will let people see the breathtaking Himalayan peaks up close. Here’s everything you need to know about this much-anticipated project. Chenab Rail Bridge To Get Viewing Decks And A Museum Standing 1,178 feet above the Chenab River, the Chenab Rail Bridge in Jammu and Kashmir is even taller than the Eiffel Tower in Paris, France. It is a massive steel and concrete railway bridge built across a deep mountain valley. It connects the Kashmir Valley with the rest of India by train. But now, the government is planning something big. According to The Times of India, the Chenab Rail Bridge is all set to become a tourist attraction, with dedicated viewing decks and a museum showcasing insights into its engineering feat and construction challenges. The viewing decks near the bridge will allow visitors to see the beautiful Chenab River flowing through a deep gorge and, yes, not to forget, the Himalayan peaks. People standing on the tall bridge will also be able to see the beautiful peaks and the surrounding landscape. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also posted a video of the bridge on his Instagram account, calling the project, “Marvellous + Ambitious.” Also Read: After 70 Years, Kolkata’s Howrah Bridge Lights Up For Durga Puja, And It’s A Sight To Behold Rail Bridge To Attract Students & Infrastructure Enthusiasts According to The Times of India, the 1,315-metre-long bridge stands 359 metres above the riverbed. Its main arch spans 467 metres. The Chenab Rail Bridge is actually one of the most important components of the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Railway Line. This line connects remote areas of Jammu and Kashmir to the national railway network. Reportedly, the viewing decks will give visitors a vantage point to appreciate the scale of the iconic bridge and lose themselves in the beauty of the surrounding mountains. The museum, on the other hand, will have photographs, technical models and digital presentations explaining how the bridge was built. It could attract students and people interested in railway infrastructure. Company inaugurated a ₹400 crore, 12 MW IT load data center in Patna. The Patna facility supports AI and cloud workloads for eastern India. Bihar government signed an LoI with CtrlS for the proposed investment. CtrlS Datacenters Ltd will invest ₹10,000 crore in Bihar to construct a 150 MW hyperscale artificial intelligence (AI) facility in Bodh Gaya . The company has signed a Letter of Intent (LoI) with the Government of Bihar for this proposed investment. This expansion includes the inauguration of a ₹400 crore data center in Patna . The Patna facility, located in the Patliputra Industrial Area, has an initial IT load of 12 MW. This facility supports AI and cloud workloads for enterprises, government institutions, hyperscalers, and technology companies across Bihar and eastern India . Advt Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary inaugurated the Patna facility on October 13, 2026. CtrlS founder and CEO Sridhar Pinnapureddy stated the company aims to build a stronger IT ecosystem in Bihar. He credited the state government's policy environment, business climate, and incentives for supporting the investment. The new data center incorporates disaster-resilient infrastructure, military-grade security, and energy-efficient systems, according to CtrlS. The company plans to establish more than 20 edge data centers across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities in India in the coming years. CtrlS operates 19 data centers across nine key Indian markets and plans to build over 4.4 GW of capacity by 2030. national_raw_news.title: 10 mins ago | National 52 India’s defence exports surge to ₹38,000 crore from ₹686 crore in last 13 years: Defence Mi...
national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said that India is exporting indigenous defence products to nearly 100 countries worldwide. He said that India’s defence exports have surged from just ₹686 crore in 2013-14 to more than ₹38,000 crore in 2025-26. Speaking at the Times Now Defence Conclave 2026 in New Delhi today, Mr Singh said, ‘India has achieved more than 90% self-reliance in Ammunition Variants. He highlighted that today, out of 175 Ammunition Variants in the Indian Army’s inventory, 159 are indigenous. The Minister said, over the past twelve and a half years, defence sector has not only expanded its capabilities but has also undergone a significant strategic shift in its approach to strengthening national security. He said that the government is building a defence ecosystem that not only strengthens national security and drives economic growth but also reinforces India’s role in the global security architecture. The Minister said, India’s armed forces are fully prepared to face any challenge. Mr Singh said that today security forces have neutralized most of the terrorists within a year of their taking up arms against India. The Minister said, Operation Sindoor, Balakot Airstrikes and Surgical Strikes were not just military operations, but they symbolised a decisive shift in the nation’s approach, moving from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action aimed at rooting out terrorism by reaching its very source. Reiterating India’s stand on cross-border terrorism, Mr Singh asserted that any further terrorist acts originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response.

national_raw_news.title: 32 mins ago | Regional News 228 Development of Ladakh is major priority for Centre: PM Modi
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said that the development of Ladakh is a major priority for the Centre. Mr Modi said this while addressing the people of Ladakh through video conferencing after inaugurating five projects worth around three thousand three hundred 50 crore rupees in the Union Territory virtually. In his address, the Prime Minister emphasised that the projects would improve connectivity, strengthen electricity infrastructure, enhance water availability and boost the preservation of Ladakh’s ancient heritage. The newly inaugurated projects include the New Passenger Terminal Building at Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport in Leh, the 298-kilometre-long Nimmu-Padum-Darcha Road, the nine-megawatt Hanu Small Hydroelectric Project, the 66-kV Double-Circuit Dah-Hanu-Khaltsi Transmission Line, India’s first Petroglyph Conservation Park at Sindhu Ghat in Leh, and 40 water bodies developed across 40 villages under Project Him Sarovar. Mr Modi described the inauguration of these projects as another chapter in Ladakh’s progress and development. He said greater attention had been given to the development needs of Ladakh after it became a Union Territory. The Prime Minister said the Centre is paying special attention to the younger generation of Ladakh, with a focus on quality education, opportunities to learn new technologies and reducing dependence on other cities. He said a major Centre of Excellence is being developed in Leh. Mr Modi added that efforts were being made to promote sporting talent through Ladakh’s new sports policy. He said the aim is to provide better training and facilities to young people so that they can achieve new milestones at national and international levels. The Prime Minister said the Centre is also focused on developing modern infrastructure while ensuring that Ladakh’s environment is protected. He added that tourism opportunities in the region are expanding, with winter and adventure tourism being promoted to generate employment. Mr Modi said greenhouse farming has also received a sustained push in Ladakh. He noted that the region now has 11,000 greenhouses, creating new opportunities to increase farmers’ incomes. Referring to the new airport terminal, the Prime Minister said geothermal technology had been used to address Ladakh’s challenging climatic conditions. He said it is the country’s first airport terminal equipped with geothermal heating facilities. The terminal, built at a cost of 640 crore rupees, covers 23,800 square metres and is designed to handle 35 lakh passengers annually. Mr Modi said it would give fresh impetus to tourism in Ladakh. The Prime Minister said the 298-kilometre Nimmu-Padum-Darcha Road would reduce travel time on the route from 12 hours to just three hours. Constructed by the Border Roads Organisation, the road connects Nimmu in Leh with Darcha in Himachal Pradesh through the remote Zanskar Valley. It provides an alternative connectivity corridor to Ladakh, supplementing the Srinagar-Leh and Manali-Leh highways. Mr Modi said the road would save travel time and provide significant support to trade and business. The Hanu Small Hydroelectric Project and the Dah-Hanu-Khaltsi Transmission Line are aimed at strengthening power evacuation infrastructure and improving the reliability of Ladakh’s electricity network. The 40 water bodies developed under Project Him Sarovar are spread across 40 villages.

national_raw_news.title: Prez Murmu calls for greater economic empowerment of rural women to achieve vision of Viksit Bharat before 2047 21 mins ago 17
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has called for greater economic empowerment of rural women, asserting that their active participation in nation-building will be crucial to achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat before 2047. The President inaugurated the National SARAS Mela 2026 in Vijayawada today in the presence of Andhra Pradesh Governor S. Abdul Nazeer, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and several Union and State Ministers. Speaking on the occasion, Ms. Murmu said that women associated with self-help groups were becoming self-reliant and contributing significantly to their families, the rural economy and national development. She said self-help groups had created livelihood opportunities for women in agriculture, animal husbandry and small businesses. Describing the SARAS Mela as an important platform for rural development, the President said it enabled women entrepreneurs to showcase their products, connect directly with consumers and access urban markets. She also highlighted efforts to promote Andhra Pradesh’s traditional crafts, including Kalamkari and toy-making, through the fair. Union Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said the target of creating three crore Lakhpati Didis had been achieved ahead of schedule. The Centre has now set a target of six crore Lakhpati Didis, with three-and-a-half crore women already achieving the milestone, he said. Mr. Chouhan highlighted the role of training, financial assistance and government support in promoting women’s economic independence. He said the SARAS Mela, being organised in Vijayawada for the first time outside Delhi, provides an important platform for self-help groups to market their products. He added that the government aims to provide better marketing opportunities in every district, with Andhra Pradesh serving as a model. Union Ministers K. Ram Mohan Naidu, Dr. Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar and Kamlesh Paswan, along with other dignitaries, officials and Lakhpati Didis, attended the event.

national_raw_news.title: PIB upholds Press Council of India's directive for journalists to report responsibly
national_raw_news.content: PIB upholds Press Council of India's directive for journalists to report responsibly | MorungExpress | morungexpress.com PIB upholds Press Council of India's directive for journalists to report responsibly PIB upholds Press Council of India's directive for journalists to report responsibly (Photo: IANS) India 15th October 2026 New Delhi, October 15 (IANS): The Press Information Bureau (PIB) on Thursday upheld the Press Council of India's (PCI) norms for journalistic conduct, urging for responsible reporting amid the alleged spread of misinformation regarding protests seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls controversy. In a post on X, the PIB said: "Responsible journalism begins with distinguishing facts from conjecture, speculation, and opinion." "As outlined in the Press Council of India’s Norms of Journalistic Conduct 2022, journalists must uphold accuracy, exercise editorial responsibility, and ensure that satire and commentary do not cross the line into defamation," it added. The PIB highlighted that the norms of journalistic conduct emphasise the importance of distinguishing facts from conjecture, speculation and opinion to ensure responsible reporting and maintain public trust. It urged journalists to not present conjecture, speculation or opinion as fact and instead clearly distinguish between them. "Cartoons and caricatures intended as good-natured humour fall into a separate category and may be treated more liberally," the PIB said while emphasizing on the norms of the Press Council of India. It cautioned that while satire is an accepted form of writing, it must not be used to disguise defamatory statements. "Words such as ‘incompetent’ or ‘impotent’ must be judged in the context of political commentary to determine whether they are offensive," the PIB added. Meanwhile, the Press Council of India has consistently advised the Press to adopt restraint and caution in its reporting. "An attempt should be made to create an environment in which, through self-regulation, the Press ensures an optimum balance between the exercise of its freedom and its responsibility. That is the basic objective Press Council seeks to promote and enshrine," the Press Council of India stated in a note on its website. As per Section 13 (b) of the Press Council Act, 1978 the Council has been mandated to build a code of conduct for newspapers, news agencies and journalists for achieving high standards of reporting. In pursuance of the same, based on the adjudications and other pronouncements rendered by it, the Council has evolved over the years, principles that are expected to be applied with due discernment and adaptation by journalists to regulate their own conduct in discharge of professional duties, as mentioned by the PCI. Earlier, Delhi Police's Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations unit registered more than four FIRs against social media handles allegedly spreading false narratives and attempting to disturb the national atmosphere. national_raw_news.title: PIB Upholds Press Council Of India's Directive For Journalists To Report Responsibly
national_raw_news.content: PIB Upholds Press Council Of India's Directive For Journalists To Report Responsibly | Nation Feedback RSS Feed Sitemap Home Odisha Nation World Sports Business Entertainment Videos Science & Tech Photo Gallery Odisha Special No Result View All Result Home Odisha Nation World Sports Business Entertainment Videos Science & Tech Photo Gallery Odisha Special No Result View All Result Home Nation PIB Upholds Press Council Of India’s Directive For Journalists To Report Responsibly by OMMCOM NEWS October 15, 2026 in Nation New Delhi: The Press Information Bureau (PIB) on Thursday upheld the Press Council of India’s (PCI) norms for journalistic conduct, urging for responsible reporting amid the alleged spread of misinformation regarding protests seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls controversy. In a post on X, the PIB said: “Responsible journalism begins with distinguishing facts from conjecture, speculation, and opinion.” “As outlined in the Press Council of India’s Norms of Journalistic Conduct 2022, journalists must uphold accuracy, exercise editorial responsibility, and ensure that satire and commentary do not cross the line into defamation,” it added. The PIB highlighted that the norms of journalistic conduct emphasise the importance of distinguishing facts from conjecture, speculation and opinion to ensure responsible reporting and maintain public trust. It urged journalists to not present conjecture, speculation or opinion as fact and instead clearly distinguish between them. “Cartoons and caricatures intended as good-natured humour fall into a separate category and may be treated more liberally,” the PIB said while emphasizing on the norms of the Press Council of India. It cautioned that while satire is an accepted form of writing, it must not be used to disguise defamatory statements. “Words such as ‘incompetent’ or ‘impotent’ must be judged in the context of political commentary to determine whether they are offensive,” the PIB added. Meanwhile, the Press Council of India has consistently advised the Press to adopt restraint and caution in its reporting. “An attempt should be made to create an environment in which, through self-regulation, the Press ensures an optimum balance between the exercise of its freedom and its responsibility. That is the basic objective Press Council seeks to promote and enshrine,” the Press Council of India stated in a note on its website. As per Section 13 (b) of the Press Council Act, 1978 the Council has been mandated to build a code of conduct for newspapers, news agencies and journalists for achieving high standards of reporting. In pursuance of the same, based on the adjudications and other pronouncements rendered by it, the Council has evolved over the years, principles that are expected to be applied with due discernment and adaptation by journalists to regulate their own conduct in discharge of professional duties, as mentioned by the PCI. Earlier, Delhi Police’s Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations unit registered more than four FIRs against social media handles allegedly spreading false narratives and attempting to disturb the national atmosphere. national_raw_news.content: “Any terror act originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response”: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर “Any terror act originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response”: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh ANI | Updated: Oct 15, 2026 14:06 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 15 (ANI): Reiterating India’s stand on cross-border terrorism, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday asserted that any further terrorist acts originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response. He emphasised that while India’s cultural ethos favoured dialogue, coexistence and peaceful resolution of disputes, its commitment to peace should not be mistaken for weakness. “Operation Sindoor, Balakot Airstrikes and Surgical Strikes weren’t just military operations; they symbolised a decisive shift in the nation’s approach, moving from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action aimed at rooting out terrorism by reaching its very source,” Singh said at the Times Network Defence Conclave in New Delhi. He added that since 2014, the ‘shelf life’ of most terrorists had fallen to less than a year, with security forces neutralising them within a year of their taking up arms against India. Defence Minister termed strength and capability as essential to maintaining peace, and underlined that India hopes for peace, but remains prepared for war that sometimes becomes necessary to protect the nation. “Our commitment to peace remains steadfast, yet we are fully prepared to confront any challenge. Our goal is to build an India that, while advocating for peace, remains vigilant when it comes to security and is fully capable of safeguarding its sovereignty, integrity, and national interests,” he said. On the evolving security landscape, Singh underscored the need for heightened vigilance and preparedness in an era of hybrid, high-tech and hyper warfare. He highlighted the growing complexity of security threats in the digital age, identifying what he described as the ‘5D Security Threat ’-Disinformation, Destabilisation, Disruption, Deception and Destruction. He pointed out that terrorism was evolving beyond organised groups, and emerging threats include ‘lone-wolf’ attacks and ‘white-collar terrorism’, which make it increasingly difficult for security agencies to identify radicalised individuals and prevent potential attacks. The Defence Minister referred to the recent incident involving a co-pilot who allegedly attempted to crash a passenger aircraft and Captain Smit Machhar who risked his life to avert a major terror attack. “The incident underscored the threat posed by lone-wolf attackers while demonstrating how the courage and commitment of an individual could thwart the designs of those driven by hatred. A single alert and courageous individual could help foil an entire terrorist plot. The fight against terrorism requires not only the capabilities of security agencies but also the active participation of aware and responsible citizens,” he said. On defence preparedness, Singh underscored the need to combine ‘hard power’ with ‘soft power’ and called for a shift towards ‘smart power’. “Modern defence strategies must integrate precision-guided weapons and loitering munitions with cost-effective weaponry, human intelligence with artificial intelligence, and advanced systems with low-cost, agile and adaptable technologies...

national_raw_news.title: Paras Health network grows 42.5% over two years, ranks 3rd nationally - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: Paras Health network grows 42.5% over two years, ranks 3rd nationally Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Paras Health network grows 42.5% over two years, ranks 3rd nationally ANI | Updated: Oct 15, 2026 13:22 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel VMPL Gurugram (Haryana) [India], October 15: IPO-bound Paras Health has been ranked joint third alongside Manipal Hospitals in the National Group Ranking 2026 for private multispeciality hospital groups. The network of eight hospitals recorded a 42.5% increase in inpatient volumes and a 31.3% rise in surgeries between FY2024 and FY2026, according to its June 2026 draft abridged prospectus. Apollo Hospitals placed first and Fortis Healthcare second. The survey assessed eligible groups as integrated networks, so Paras’s position applies to the group as a whole rather than to individual hospitals. The ranking comes as organised private hospital chains expand through new facilities, additional beds and acquisitions. ICRA’s July 2026 update projected revenue growth of 13–15% in FY2027 for its sample of hospital companies, following 18% growth in FY2026. Separately, Crisil Ratings’ February assessment of 98 private hospitals forecast more than 10,000 bed additions through new facilities and expansions of existing hospitals across FY2026 and FY2027. Expansion is taking place alongside improving financial coverage and continuing pressure on households. The government’s 2025 health survey found insurance or financing-scheme coverage had reached 47.4% in rural India and 44.3% in urban areas. National Health Accounts estimates for FY2022–23, released in May 2026, show households still paid 43.4% of total health expenditure directly. For hospital networks, these figures underline the importance of affordability and access alongside increasing capacity. ( pib.gov.in , pib.gov.in ) Hospital chains also face the task of recruiting and retaining specialist doctors and nurses, developing referral systems and maintaining reliable diagnostics. As networks grow, providers must balance spending on clinical teams, equipment and new facilities with the need to keep treatment accessible and sustain standards across locations. Dr Dharminder Kumar Nagar, Managing Director, Paras Health, said, “Sharing third place in the national hospital group ranking is an important milestone for Paras Health. Our growth in inpatient volumes and surgeries brings a responsibility to strengthen the clinical teams and infrastructure supporting that care. We are focused on building specialist capabilities and critical care capacity across our hospitals, while maintaining consistent standards as more patients use our network.” Paras’s inpatient volumes reached 115,496 in FY2026, compared with 81,047 in FY2024. The filing counts patients admitted and subsequently discharged during the relevant period. Surgeries increased to 39,687 from 30,219, while outpatient consultation visits rose 36.8% to 778,707 from 569,139 over the same two years. Revenue from operations increased 24.1% year on year to approximately ₹1,606 crore in FY2026 from ₹1,294 crore in FY2025. The group reported a consolidated profit after tax of ₹43.83 crore in FY2026, compared with a loss of ₹57.98 crore a year earlier. Overall bed occupancy rose to 61.75% in FY2026 from 52.46% in FY2024. As of March 31, 2026, Paras reported 1,502 operational beds, up from 1,332 two years earlier. ICU...
